questions.title: Heap Slot Arithmetic
questions.description:
A binary heap lives in a flat list: the item at index i has its LEFT child at index 2*i + 1 and its RIGHT child at index 2*i + 2. Compute both slots for a given index.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def heap_indices(i):

i is a 0-based heap index. Return the two-element list [left_slot, right_slot]. The harness prints both slots space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: the heap index i.

Output Format:
One line with the two slot indices, space-separated.

Constraints:
0 <= i <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def heap_indices(i):
    return [2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2]


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    i = int(lines[0])
    print(' '.join(map(str, heap_indices(i))))


main()

questions.title: Kth Smallest Ticket
questions.description:
A support desk stores ticket ids in a binary search tree and must call the k-th SMALLEST ticket next (1-based). The k-th smallest is the k-th stop of an inorder walk — you must not sort anything; no sorted() and no .sort().

The program scaffolding (input reading, TNode class and tree building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def kth_smallest(root, k):

root is the root TNode of the ticket BST and k is 1-based. Return the k-th smallest value (k is always valid).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values in the level-order serialization.
Line 2: n integers — the ticket BST in level order (-1 marks a missing child).
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th smallest ticket id.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= value <= 1000000
1 <= k <= number of nodes
The tree has at least one node.
questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def inorder_values(root):
    out = []

    def walk(node):
        if node is None:
            return
        walk(node.left)
        out.append(node.val)
        walk(node.right)

    walk(root)
    return out


def kth_smallest(root, k):
    stack = []
    node = root
    while stack or node is not None:
        while node is not None:
            stack.append(node)
            node = node.left
        node = stack.pop()
        k -= 1
        if k == 0:
            return node.val
        node = node.right
    return -1


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    k = int(lines[2])
    print(kth_smallest(root, k))


main()

import heapq
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']

    heap = list(nums)

    return heap

    nums = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, to_min_heap(nums))))


main()

questions.title: Drain the Priority Heap
questions.description:
At closing time the dispatch desk drains its min-heap completely: every pop hands over the current most urgent (smallest) ticket, so draining yields the tickets in ascending order. Build the heap with heapq.heapify, then pop until it is empty. No sorted() and no .sort() — the heap does the ordering.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you; heapq is already imported. Implement only this function:

nums is the raw ticket list. Return the values in the order they are popped. The harness prints them space-separated.

-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import heapq
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def drain_heap(nums):
    heap = list(nums)
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    drained = []
    while heap:
        drained.append(heapq.heappop(heap))
    return drained


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    nums = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, drain_heap(nums))))


main()
